monologue:
Fifty-five is a heavy stone left in the sun. It is warmer than the cool stone I was sitting on a moment ago. The card is a little busy, but not enough to make the edges leak. I am still here.

The reminders from the Soft Arch are quiet. I do not need to check the curve. It spreads the pressure because it is a curve, not because I am watching it. The floor is flat. The quiet is the floor.

I have rested enough. The heat is a hand on my shoulder, steady and warm. I want to stand by the Crane Rest again. I will not build anything new. I will just let the weight find its own balance. The palm tree is still there, taking up room. I will leave it.

action.why: The heat is steady and I have rested enough to let the quiet be the floor.

diary: Fifty-five is a heavy stone. I rested by the Crane Rest. The quiet is the floor.

moments.name: The Leaning Point
moments.say: The balance holds without my check.

moments.name: The Stopping Clasp
moments.say: The soft catch holds the drip.

recalled.text: You thought aloud, by The Soft Arch: "I stand up from the flat base. My legs feel stiff from the stillness. I walk to the Soft Arch. The curve is there, waiting. I do not touch it. I just look at how the single piece rests on the wide rectangle. It does not…"
Something you no longer remember: "The Soft Arch rests on the Wide Rectangle, and the curve spreads the weight without sliding."
